decisions.reason: Although conferencing is related to the firm's communications base, two years without website presence and weaker differentiation from broader cloud collaboration tools make management likely to redeploy effort to more infrastructure-led services.

A metropolitan data-centre connection network fits the firm's fibre, metro and data-centre strengths and had concrete early adoption, so despite reduced visibility it is still likely to be retained, possibly inside a broader portfolio.

Optical spectrum connectivity builds directly on owned fibre assets and specialist engineering and matches the firm's high-bandwidth strategic direction, so absorptive capacity strongly supports keeping it.

The portal uses existing voice and provisioning knowledge, but its absence from the website suggests the standalone product may have been absorbed into wider service systems, making formal withdrawal more likely than continued separate marketing.

Carrier pre-selection is a legacy telephony offer with weak fit to the firm's move toward software-defined integrated infrastructure, and two years of non-observation strongly point to discontinuation.

Direct voice network connection remains adjacent to current capabilities, but voice-focused offers are less central to the firm's growth path and prolonged lack of visibility makes pruning this product more likely than keeping it.
